# Abstract

- drought read as a queue of unmet irrigation demand
- arrivals $\lambda(t)$ from climate demand, service $\mu(t)$ from streamflow
- backlog $Q$, finite capacity $K$, reneging, severe-state threshold $q^\star$
- queue-state indicators: $\mathbb{E}[Q]$, $\Pr(Q \ge q^\star)$, unmet volume, recovery time
- one identical protocol in India (CAMELS-IND) and the USA (Caravan-US)
- catchment unit; catchment SPEI-3 target from own precipitation and Hargreaves ET0
- same demand ($K_c = 0.8$, $f_{\text{irr}} = 0.10$), same supply (SUP-1), same split (1981--2010 / 2011--2020)
- same screen, same eight families, same paired Brier contrast, same two-level bootstrap
- engine verified against exact stationary solution, RK4 and Gillespie simulation (15/15 checks)
- result India: `r f4(getv("SPEI-3","India","median_delta"))` median $\Delta$Brier, 95% CI [`r f4(getv("SPEI-3","India","boot_lo"))`, `r f4(getv("SPEI-3","India","boot_hi"))`], `r getv("SPEI-3","India","sign_k")`/`r getv("SPEI-3","India","sign_n")` catchments improve
- result USA: `r f4(getv("SPEI-3","USA","median_delta"))`, 95% CI [`r f4(getv("SPEI-3","USA","boot_lo"))`, `r f4(getv("SPEI-3","USA","boot_hi"))`], `r getv("SPEI-3","USA","sign_k")`/`r getv("SPEI-3","USA","sign_n")`
- region difference: `r f4(dtab[target=="SPEI-3"]$difference)`, 95% CI [`r f4(dtab[target=="SPEI-3"]$diff_lo)`, `r f4(dtab[target=="SPEI-3"]$diff_hi)`]
- SPI-3 sensitivity target: India `r f4(getv("SPI-3","India","median_delta"))`, USA `r f4(getv("SPI-3","USA","median_delta"))`
- no general calibrated-probability advantage; a small, target-consistent signal in the larger US sample
- contributions: one common protocol; one verified engine; one small, sample-dependent signal; one zero-flow data-quality warning

# Introduction

## Drought as a deficit, not only an index

- drought is a persistent water deficit with meteorological, agricultural, hydrological and socio-economic faces (Wilhite & Glantz, 1985; Mishra & Singh, 2010)
- hydrological drought is the slowest to develop and the slowest to recover (Tallaksen & Van Lanen, 2004; Van Loon, 2015)
- operational practice compresses the deficit into an index
- SPI from precipitation (McKee et al., 1993)
- SPEI from precipitation minus potential evapotranspiration (Vicente-Serrano et al., 2010)
- SSI from streamflow; review in Heim (2002)
- indices answer "how dry", not "how much demand is unmet, for how long, and how close to failure"
- the missing object is the accumulated deficit state and its capacity

## The queue analogy is old, and that matters

- storage theory was framed as queueing theory by Langbein (1958)
- reservoir storage as a queue, inflow as arrivals, release as service
- the analogy was reclaimed, not discovered, here
- queueing returned to hydrology through runoff--runon (Harel & Mouche, 2013, 2014; Mouche & Harel, 2016; Jones et al., 2016)
- groundwater management as a queue (Batabyal, 1996)
- irrigation allocation as a queue (Prajamwong et al., 1997; Yang et al., 2016)
- time-varying and correlated arrival queues are well developed (Bogachev et al., 2023, 2024)
- learning and control for queues is a mature field (Asanjarani et al., 2021)
- therefore the novelty is not "queues in hydrology" and not "learning queues"
- the open junction is hydrological parameterisation + deficit interpretation + exact validation + pre-specified drought tests

## What this paper does

- reads drought as a finite-capacity queue of unmet irrigation demand
- estimates $\lambda(t)$ from catchment climate (precipitation and Hargreaves ET0) and $\mu(t)$ from observed streamflow
- reports queue-state quantities as drought quantities
- tests the queue against SSI-3 on a catchment SPEI-3 target
- applies exactly one protocol in two regions
- reports a small US signal, a null in India, and no regional difference
- reports the engine as a reusable contribution
- reports a zero-flow data-quality warning
- the frozen scope statement (21 November 2026, quoted verbatim):
  "Within Crossref, OpenAlex, the complete WoS S1--S5 / Extra A/B/C screens (142 records) and the completed Scopus S1--S5 / Extra A/C screens (295 records), plus the citation traces, we found no study that puts all four of these together: (1) drought as an accumulated unmet-demand backlog with a finite-capacity state; (2) queue-state indicators reported as drought quantities; (3) non-stationary rates estimated from hydroclimatic covariates; (4) validation against exact reference solutions and pre-specified drought tests."
- hypotheses, fixed before the common run
- H1: adding queue state to SSI-3 lowers the paired Brier score for SPEI-3 drought
- H2 (exploratory): the improvement is larger where utilisation $\rho$ is higher
- H3: the result is the same in both regions

# Data

- India: CAMELS-IND, 472 gauges, daily precipitation, minimum/maximum/mean temperature and streamflow (Mangukiya et al., 2025)
- USA: Caravan-US, 671 gauges, the same variables (Kratzert et al., 2023)
- unit: gauge catchment in both regions
- catchment area explicit: $A_{\text{cmd}} = f_{\text{irr}} A_{\text{catchment}}$, $f_{\text{irr}} = 0.10$
- one claim is $d = 20$ mm over $A_{\text{cmd}}$
- no district soil-moisture product
- no US Drought Monitor
- no reservoir record
- no remote-sensing evapotranspiration
- period 1981--2020; training 1981--2010, test 2011--2020

# Methods

## Demand rate

- Hargreaves--Samani reference ET0 from temperature range and extraterrestrial radiation (Hargreaves & Samani, 1985)
- no radiation input, so the same equation is valid in both regions
- daily unmet depth: $\text{need}(t) = \max[K_c \mathrm{ET}_0(t) - \phi P(t), 0]$
- common crop coefficient $K_c = 0.8$ [assumption]
- effective-rain fraction $\phi = 0.7$ [assumption]
- arrival rate $\lambda(t) = \text{need}(t)/d$, in claims per day

## Supply rate

- observed flow $Q(t)$ in m$^3$ s$^{-1}$
- firm share $s_{\text{firm}} = 0.5$ [assumption]
- delivery cap 10 mm day$^{-1}$ [assumption]
- $\mu(t) = d^{-1}\min\{Q(t)\,86400\,s_{\text{firm}} A_{\text{cmd}}^{-1} 1000,\ \text{cap}\}$

## Queue state

- finite-capacity continuous-time birth--death chain on $Q \in \{0,\dots,K\}$
- Poisson arrivals and exponential service [assumption]
- reneging at rate $\eta$ above threshold $\theta$
- service boost $\alpha$ above $\theta$
- thresholds: $q^\star = \lceil 60\bar\lambda\rceil$, $K = \min\{80,\max(25,\lceil 365\bar\lambda\rceil)\}$, $\theta = \lceil 1.5 q^\star\rceil$
- parameters $\alpha = 1.5$, $\eta = 1/60$ day$^{-1}$
- solved by RK4 with the stability cap $\Delta t\,\max|\text{eigenvalue}| \le 2.78$
- exact stationary solution from the product form
- discrete-event Gillespie/thinning simulation as the third check
- 15/15 verification checks in `R/verify.R`

## Target and benchmark indices

- SPEI-3 from the catchment's own $P$ and $\mathrm{ET}_0$ (Vicente-Serrano et al., 2010)
- three-month accumulation $D_3(t) = \sum_{i=0}^{2}[P(t-i) - \mathrm{ET}_0(t-i)]$
- standardized per calendar month on training years only
- target $Y(t) = 1[\text{SPEI-3}(t) \le -1]$
- SPI-3 from precipitation, gamma fit per calendar month on training years (McKee et al., 1993)
- SSI-3 from $\log(1+Q)$, standardized per calendar month on training years
- standardization on training years only keeps the target leakage-free

## Screen and design

- utilisation $\rho = \bar\lambda/\bar\mu$ in $[0.15, 1.20]$
- zero-flow fraction below 0.30
- largest interior gap at most 30 days
- at least 1095 training days and 730 test days
- at least 5 training and 3 test design events
- at most 3 catchments per basin (US basin = HUC4)
- at most 60 catchments per region
- missing days never interpolated
- a missing day pauses the queue
- any month containing a missing day is excluded from indices and target
- eight model families, ridge logistic regression with month dummies
- standardized on training rows only
- confirmatory contrast $\Delta_g = \text{Brier}_g(\text{SSI-3}) - \text{Brier}_g(\text{SSI-3 + queue})$
- paired on identical held-out months
- median over catchments with a two-level bootstrap (gauges, then years)
- one-sided sign test reported alongside
- SPEI-3 primary; SPI-3 sensitivity; families using SPEI-3 as a predictor are descriptive only

- USA sign test `r getv("SPEI-3","USA","sign_k")`/`r getv("SPEI-3","USA","sign_n")`, $p = `r fp(getv("SPEI-3","USA","sign_p"))`$

- the difference interval includes zero

## Sensitivity target: catchment SPI-3

- India: `r f4(getv("SPI-3","India","median_delta"))`, 95% CI [`r f4(getv("SPI-3","India","boot_lo"))`, `r f4(getv("SPI-3","India","boot_hi"))`], `r getv("SPI-3","India","sign_k")`/`r getv("SPI-3","India","sign_n")`
- USA: `r f4(getv("SPI-3","USA","median_delta"))`, 95% CI [`r f4(getv("SPI-3","USA","boot_lo"))`, `r f4(getv("SPI-3","USA","boot_hi"))`], `r getv("SPI-3","USA","sign_k")`/`r getv("SPI-3","USA","sign_n")`
- region difference `r f4(dtab[target=="SPI-3"]$difference)`, 95% CI [`r f4(dtab[target=="SPI-3"]$diff_lo)`, `r f4(dtab[target=="SPI-3"]$diff_hi)`]
- the SPI-3 target is a precipitation-only deficit; SPEI-3 also includes the evaporative demand that drives $\lambda(t)$

## Utilisation

- the utilisation window is a screening rule, not a result
- exploratory link between $\rho$ and $\Delta$Brier within each region

```{r util-corr}
corr_one <- function(reg) {
  s <- fread(OUT(sprintf("%s_screen.csv", reg)))
  p <- fread(OUT(sprintf("%s_paired.csv", reg)))
  m <- merge(
    s[, .(gauge_id = as.character(gauge_id), rho)],
    p[, .(gauge_id = as.character(gauge_id), delta_brier)],
    by = "gauge_id")
  m <- m[is.finite(rho) & is.finite(delta_brier)]
  if (nrow(m) < 5) return(c(estimate = NA_real_, p.value = NA_real_, n = nrow(m)))
  ct <- suppressWarnings(stats::cor.test(m$rho, m$delta_brier, method = "spearman"))
  c(estimate = unname(ct$estimate), p.value = ct$p.value, n = nrow(m))
}
ci <- corr_one("india"); cu <- corr_one("usa")
```

- India Spearman $\rho_s = `r sprintf("%+.2f", ci["estimate"])`$, $p = `r fp(ci["p.value"])`$, $n = `r ci["n"]`$
- USA Spearman $\rho_s = `r sprintf("%+.2f", cu["estimate"])`$, $p = `r fp(cu["p.value"])`$, $n = `r cu["n"]`$
- this is descriptive and was not part of the confirmatory contrast

```{r fig-utilisation, fig.cap="Distribution of catchment utilisation $\\rho = \\bar\\lambda/\\bar\\mu$ in the two regions. Shaded band is the predeclared admissible window 0.15--1.20.", out.width="92%"}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIG_DIR, "fig_utilisation.pdf"))
```

# Discussion

## What the result says

- under one common protocol the queue does not add a general calibrated-probability gain
- a small positive signal appears in the larger US sample for SPEI-3
- the same contrast is null in the 12-catchment India sample
- the region difference is not distinguishable from zero
- the sign is consistent with target alignment: SPEI-3 is a climate water deficit, and the queue demand is also a climate water deficit
- the effect is small: about `r f4(getv("SPEI-3","USA","median_delta"))` Brier units
- ranking changes little: median $\Delta$AUC `r f4(getv("SPEI-3","USA","median_dauc"))` in the USA

## Why the earlier larger signal does not survive

- earlier work on the same data used a district soil-moisture target and a kharif demand envelope
- both choices are region-specific and were removed here
- the common protocol uses a constant $K_c = 0.8$ and a catchment SPEI-3 target
- once the method is identical, the large target-dependent gain disappears
- this is the point of the comparability test, not a failure of the queue

## What the queue still gives

- an explicit backlog state $Q$
- severe-state probability $\Pr(Q \ge q^\star)$
- unmet-volume accounting through the conservation ledger
- recovery time from first passage
- these are descriptive quantities that indices do not provide
- Langbein's storage analogy is thereby made operational at catchment scale
- the engine is reusable beyond this test (Harel & Mouche, 2013; Mouche & Harel, 2016)

## Assumptions and limits

- demand is a Stage-A envelope, not measured irrigation
- $K_c$, $\phi$, $s_{\text{firm}}$ and the cap are stated assumptions
- Poisson arrivals and exponential service
- Hargreaves ET0 is temperature-based
- SPEI-3 and SSI-3 are catchment-scale proxies, not management records
- 12 India catchments give a wide interval
- the 60-catchment US cap trades power for balance
- zero-flow days in CAMELS-IND may be measured no-flow or a coding convention
- zeros are used as recorded; the alternative must be reported alongside

## What would change the answer

- measured irrigation deliveries for $\lambda(t)$
- independent canal and reservoir operation records for $\mu(t)$ and $K$
- a strictly external drought benchmark not derived from the same climate inputs
- a larger paired sample in India
- a pre-specified test in a third region

# Conclusion

- a deficit queue is a coherent way to state what drought costs in unmet demand
- it is not a general replacement for calibrated SPI, SPEI or SSI probabilities
- under one identical protocol, the gain is small in the USA and absent in India
- the durable contributions are the common protocol, the verified engine and the data-quality warning
- the frozen novelty sentence is unchanged
- the result is reported as a small, sample-dependent signal, not a universal win
